exposure: Unplanned conversion to general anesthesia during elective cesarean section
cohort: 4337 women who underwent elective cesarean section at a UK center between 2008 and 2013
finding: Higher parity and maternal age were identified as risk factors for unplanned conversion to general anesthesia during elective cesarean section.
mod_finding: Unplanned conversion to general anesthesia was associated with increased likelihood of maternal hemorrhage and delayed neonatal respiration compared to spinal anesthesia, but adverse outcomes were not significantly more likely compared with planned general anesthesia.
